adjudicated_statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let C be a smooth projective connected curve over k and let gamma : C -> P^1 be a finite morphism of degree four. Call gamma simply branched when every geometric fibre has at most one ramification point and that point, if present, has ramification index two; equivalently, every local monodromy permutation in S_4 is a transposition. (a) No such gamma that factors nontrivially through an intermediate smooth projective curve is simply branched. A nontrivial factorization is a pair of finite morphisms C -> Y -> P^1 each of degree at least two (necessarily both of degree two); equivalently, k(C)/k(P^1) is composite of two proper extensions and the monodromy representation of pi_1^et(P^1 minus the branch locus of gamma) in S_4 is imprimitive. Two independent reasons. First: a simply branched connected degree-four cover has all local monodromies transpositions, so its monodromy group G <= S_4 is transitive and generated by transpositions. A transitive subgroup of S_n generated by transpositions equals S_n, because the undirected graph on n letters with those transpositions as edges is connected and the transpositions of a connected graph generate S_n. Thus G = S_4, which is primitive on four letters. A nontrivial factorization supplies a G-invariant partition of a general fibre into two blocks of size two, so G lies in a conjugate of the imprimitive wreath product S_2 wr S_2 of order 8, contradicting G = S_4. (The wreath product contains the two within-block transpositions, but those generate an intransitive Klein subgroup; transitivity of an imprimitive degree-four group requires a block-swapping element, necessarily a double transposition or a 4-cycle.) Second, without invoking S_4: any degree-two morphism q : Y -> P^1 from a smooth projective connected curve Y is ramified, since Riemann-Hurwitz gives 2g_Y-2 = 2(-2)+deg R_q, hence deg R_q = 2g_Y+2 >= 2. Over each branch value of q the fibre of gamma = q o psi is of type (2,2) if psi is etale over the unique point of Y above it, or of type 4 (local monodromy a 4-cycle; locally the composition of two simple ramified double covers is z |-> z^4) if psi is ramified there; neither fibre is a transposition. (b) Specialise to the FND-0154 balanced type-(ii) family: Y a smooth genus-one curve, P in Pic^2(Y), q = phi_{|P|} : Y -> P^1 the associated finite flat degree-two morphism (four ramification points), M in Pic^5(Y), B a reduced divisor in |M^{otimes 2}| of degree ten, psi : C -> Y the double cover with psi_* O_C isomorphic to O_Y direct-sum M^{-1} branched along B, and gamma = q o psi. Assume in addition that B is disjoint from Ram(q) and that sigma(B) cap B is empty for the unique nontrivial deck involution sigma of q. Then the branch locus of gamma consists of exactly fourteen points of P^1: ten of fibre type 2+1+1 (local monodromy a transposition, over q(b) for b in B) and four of fibre type (2,2) (local monodromy a double transposition, over the four branch values of q, because psi is etale above each q-ramification point so both of its preimages acquire ramification index two). In characteristic zero the different has multiplicity d_x = e_x-1 at each ramification point, so the total ramification is 10*1 + 4*2 = 18. This agrees with Riemann-Hurwitz 2g_C-2 = 4(2g_{P^1}-2)+deg R, i.e. 10 = -8 + deg R. If B meets Ram(q), the corresponding fibre of gamma is a single point of ramification index four, with local monodromy a 4-cycle. If B contains a sigma-pair, the two would-be transposition fibres over q(b) and q(sigma(b)) coincide as a single extra (2,2) fibre. In particular the set of simply branched type-(ii) points is empty, so no deformation argument that requires eighteen distinct simple branch values, or etaleness of the fixed-target Hurwitz scheme over Conf_18 at a type-(ii) point, can apply to any point of the FND-0154 parameter space. This statement asserts neither that every type-(ii) point of the ambient fixed-target balanced Hurwitz scheme lies on a component meeting type (i), nor any Hodge, weight, purity, Tate, stack-inertia, or RED-0001 conclusion.
contradiction_resolution: The contested passage is ATT-0111 Section 8, second paragraph, the argument for CLM-0111-9's second half. It claims that a general reduced B in the FND-0154 family avoids Ram(q) and its q-involute, and that then gamma has eighteen distinct simple branch values, so the fixed-target Hurwitz scheme is etale over Conf_18 and smooth of dimension 18 at that point. That branch count is false at every such B, not merely generically: the profile is fourteen points of P^1 (ten of type 2+1+1 and four of type (2,2)) with total different degree 18. REV-0156 correctly isolated this error and recorded that the follow-up 'connect to a simply branched type-(ii) point inside the reduced-divisor parameter space' is vacuous because every point of that parameter space is composed. Independent check of the group theory: Pirola-Schlesinger arXiv:math/0312375v2 Remark 2.2 and Proposition 2.9 prove that a cover is decomposable if and only if its Galois group is imprimitive; that a simple branch point has transposition monodromy; and that a transitive subgroup of S_d generated by transpositions is S_d, so a simply branched connected cover is uniform (monodromy S_d) and therefore indecomposable. Kanev arXiv:math/0509154 defines a simple degree-d cover by the fibre-cardinality condition d-1 <= #pi^{-1}(y) <= d and takes the Hurwitz space H^0_{d,n} to parametrize simply branched covers with monodromy S_d. Independent check of the ramification arithmetic: Stacks Project tag 0C1D (Lemma 53.12.2) gives 2g_X-2=(2g_Y-2)deg(f)+deg(R), and tag 0C1F gives d_x=e_x-1 in characteristic zero; the elliptic double cover then has four ramification points, matching the classical Weierstrass example. Locally, composition of two simple ramified double covers is z |-> z^4, a 4-cycle, while psi etale over a q-ramification point yields fibre type (2,2). No contradiction with corroborated packet findings. FND-0153 already records that type-(ii) gamma is non-primitive and factors through genus one, but it does not treat simple branching or the fourteen-point profile; this finding is the ramification consequence of that non-primitivity, not a duplicate, and must not be merged. FND-0154 supplies the family used in (b) and does not claim simple branching. FND-0155 concerns S_6-monodromy of the six-point ordering cover, not S_4-monodromy of gamma. CLM-0111-9's first half (purely type-(ii) carrying bases exist, e.g. S=Spec k) is untouched. CLM-0111-9's second-half conclusion is not refuted; REV-0156 records it as unproved by the broken argument, with a proposed repair in the sibling candidate FC-REV0156-HURWITZ-Nsheaf-SMOOTH, which is a different statement (smoothness of the fixed-target Hurwitz stack of dimension 2d+2g-2 at every branching profile) and must not be merged. No claim in data/claims.jsonl addresses ramification of composed tetragonal covers. The original candidate text is narrowed by defining simply branched, stating the connected-graph/Serre generation lemma, recording that S_2 wr S_2 transpositions are intransitive as a generating set, adding the direct Riemann-Hurwitz argument that any degree-two map to P^1 is ramified, and restricting part (b) to the FND-0154 hypotheses. With those corrections the statement is elementary and independently verified, and should be promoted.

hypotheses: k algebraically closed of characteristic zero (tame ramification d_x=e_x-1)
nontrivial factorization means both maps finite of degree at least two, necessarily 2 then 2
simply branched means every geometric fibre has partition type 2+1+1+1, i.e. local monodromy a transposition
part (b) additionally: B reduced, B disjoint from Ram(q), and sigma(B) cap B empty
scope.part_a: any connected finite degree-four cover of P^1 from a smooth projective curve over k; not restricted to genus six
scope.part_b: the FND-0154 balanced type-(ii) family: Y elliptic, q of degree two, psi a double cover branched along a reduced divisor B of degree ten, gamma=q o psi
